slice: explore WI-d6c086 step MEASURE - Audio8-TTS 0.1B ONNX INT8 on Apple Silicon CPU

machine.power: AC; no thermal-throttle instrumentation; other user processes not quiesced

backend.onnxruntime: 1.24.4 (bench venv; NOT the 1.27.0 obey-voice links via sherpa-onnx-go)

model.reference_voice: packaged reference_codes.npy (110 frames, Chinese reference text)

harness.why: the vendor's published onnx_runtime/ code CANNOT run these graphs: it expects a transformer slow model with per-layer cache_key_N inputs, while the published slow graph is a mamba/SSM hybrid taking cache_keys/cache_values/conv_states/ssm_states, and it does not handle slow_logits_layout=relative_semantic_then_eos
harness.location: scripts/audio8_bench/ (this repo) - README.md there maps each command to a section of this artifact
harness.vendor_helpers: arktts_runtime tokenizer/prompt code from github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS @ c856e38 (Apache-2.0); only Encode/prompt-build and _sample are reused, no graph driving
harness.reproduced: 2026-08-27, vendored scripts re-run against the pinned snapshot: identical frame counts and audio durations, RTF 0.75x/1.16x vs 0.68x/1.09x recorded (run-to-run machine noise; machine not quiesced)
harness.protocol: N7 protocol - same two phrases as TestKokoroRealtimeFactor, warmup then median of 3
harness.rtf_definition: audio_seconds / total_synth_seconds (higher is faster; matches N7/F7)

baseline_same_session.note: re-measured 2026-08-27, NOT quoted from N7 (which printed 1.32x/1.38x on a quieter machine)

prefix_cache_experiment.detail: 43 system text tokens + 110 reference-voice frames, identical every turn

codec_scaling.note: codec decode is perfectly LINEAR in frames with no fixed overhead - ~12.3 ms/frame across 6..140 frames
codec_scaling.consequence: the vendor's stream() re-decodes a 128-frame context window every 12 frames, so it does ~5x more codec work than necessary. Context size is the critical streaming knob.

cached_and_pipelined_MEASURED.what: prefix cache (prime the 153-token constant head once per process) + codec decoded on a worker thread concurrently with the AR loop
cached_and_pipelined_MEASURED.config: AR 5 threads, codec 10 threads, chunk_frames=12, stream context=0
cached_and_pipelined_MEASURED.tuning_sweep: AR/codec thread splits (4/4, 5/5, 6/6, 4/8) and chunk_frames=24 were all worse. chunk=24 roughly doubles TTFA (~900 ms vs ~550) without improving total.
cached_and_pipelined_MEASURED.caveat: codec_busy exceeds AR time in every configuration, so the codec is the bottleneck even at ctx=0, and the two threads contend for CPU (AR slows from 504 ms sequential to 550 ms pipelined).

verdict.as_shipped: FAILS the N7 bar - 2.17 s for one sentence against a >1.8 s loses rule; RTF 0.68x, slower than realtime
verdict.cached_and_pipelined_MEASURED: PASSES the bar - 997 ms for one sentence, RTF 1.49x; two sentences 2031 ms, RTF 2.03x
verdict.vs_kokoro_same_session: wall-clock is a near tie (997 vs 1014 ms one sentence; 2031 vs 2078 ms two sentences) while RTF is better (1.49x vs 1.17x, 2.03x vs 1.32x) because Audio8 produces more audio for the same text
verdict.batching_threshold_2_3x: NOT cleared in any measured configuration. Closest is 2.03x on two sentences. D009 and D010 stand.
verdict.ttfa: ~550 ms to first audio via the streaming path, roughly constant across utterance length. Kokoro's TTFA was NOT measured, so no comparison is claimed.
verdict.prediction_misses: two, both recorded: pre-measurement arithmetic said 1.72x (counted only the AR loop, ignored prefill and codec); the post-measurement projection said ~3.2x cached+pipelined (assumed perfect overlap, ignored CPU contention and chunk overhead). Measured is 1.49x/2.03x.

cost_decomposition_one_sentence_ms.comment: AR decode alone is 504 ms for 1.486 s of audio = 2.95x realtime. The AR loop is FAST. Prefill and codec are what fail the bar, and prefill is the cacheable one.

open: English quality unjudged - the packaged reference voice is Chinese; no English reference was registered. run_bench.py/pipelined.py write ear-check WAVs to the working directory
CoreML EP untested for the codec, which is the bottleneck
peak RSS 2.0 GB measured vs ~0.6 GB claimed on the model card
measured against onnxruntime 1.24.4; obey-voice links 1.27.0 via sherpa-onnx-go
ctx=0 chunking was not ear-checked for boundary artifacts - it is the fastest and the least safe
prefix cache is per-process and per-reference-voice; switching voices re-pays the ~1.0 s prime
